## Open

### T-595 — prune and restart are the compaction levels still unwired

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The survey that produced the compaction levels, kept for the parts that are not the default.
Summarising is the default level and is wired with the MVP (@@D-728). What is left is `prune`, the
AI SDK `pruneMessages` plus `prepareStep`, a transient trim of reasoning and old tool calls that
leaves the checkpoint untouched and costs no model turn; and `restart`, which is a step ceiling, a
commit of the workspace and a successor session whose opening prompt carries the last answer and the
commit summary, so the code state is the context. The engine-native routes stay unused for reasons
that do not change: Mastra needs `@mastra/memory`, which is not installed, and a stored thread that
a one-shot step engine never keeps, and the DeepSeek harness compacts through a plugin its own
`cordis.yml` composes in the home the container mounts, with no knob in the SDK client.

### T-596 — Compaction levels ship unwired in the MVP

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The persona table carries `compaction`, `compactionTokens`, `compactionKeep`, `compactionModel` and
the session carries `compactedAt` and `compactionCount`, but no handler writes them:
`agentSessionCompact` is not written, so every level behaves as off. Summarising is the default
level and the one to build first (@@D-728): at the threshold, condense the transcript up to the last
kept turns, write the next checkpoint with the summary at its head, and count the crossing on the
session. The threshold has to be estimated locally from the transcript until the engine result
carries usage (@@T-594).

### T-745 — a dispatched error loses its code, leaving only the message

> _2026-11-20 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The same refusal reaches a caller in two shapes: in-process the declared error travels with its code
(`agentWorkspaceMissing`), and over a dispatch only the rendered message does
(`Workspace /srv/elsewhere/T-1005 is not on this host`). A client cannot branch on a code it does
not receive, so check whether a dispatched error is meant to keep its code, and either carry it in
the payload the dispatcher returns or state in the error docs that a cross-service caller reads the
message. Found while running `blong realm/blong-agent/index.ts dev integration`, where the ticket
group's assertion on `failure.code` fell through to the message; the assertion is now
case-insensitive rather than fixed at the cause.

### T-812 — The recovery group's refused-session step fails on its own

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · open_

`test.agent.recovery` fails at `aRefusedSessionIsPurgedAndItsTicketClosed` while every other group
in the realm is green, and it fails the same way with the feed group removed from the watch list, so
it is not a side effect of that work. It is also why the package's whole test run is red:
`node --run ci-test` reports 163 of 164, and the one failure is this step, reported twice because
`test/lukaot.reach.test.ts` drives the same integration suite.

The assertion is precise: the session ends `suspended` where the step expects `failed`. So the tick
ran a call with an account that cannot answer, the engine parked instead of refusing, and the
recovery scan - which is what the step says should have purged the session and closed its ticket -
treated a suspended session as one to keep. Decide which is right before changing anything: a
missing account is a refusal (the session fails and the ticket goes back), and a suspension is what
a question to a human looks like, so either the engine adapter should not park when the account is
missing, or the scan's rule is wrong about which suspensions it may purge. Then fix the half that
the reasoning names and put the group back in the watch list.

### T-818 — A manual trigger cannot seed its own task, because the ticket pool has no gateway surface

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · open_

A manual trigger cannot give the run a task of its own: `agent.ticket.claim` is reachable through
the gateway, but the pool it takes from is the realm's in-process fixture (`adapter/task/`, with
`task.pool.reset` and `task.ticket.edit`), and the gateway serves only the methods its own layer
validates — `task.*` has no validation and answers `Not Found`, while a plain body is refused
earlier with `gateway.mleUndecoded` because the route requires no auth. So `scripts/runTask.sh`
claims the first free ticket and sends the task as `agent.session.run`'s prompt, which means the
session row is named after the fixture's ticket rather than after the task, and five runs exhaust
the pool until the backend restarts. One of three things fixes it: a gateway validation for the
pool's two write methods, gated to `dev` so a deployment never exposes a fixture; a `blong-dev` verb
that dispatches into the running process rather than over the gateway; or the pool becoming the real
`blong-task`-backed component the adapter's header promises, where a ticket is a row a person can
write. The third is the one `D-707` is aiming at; the first is what makes this script readable until
then.

### T-594 — Engine results carry no token usage

> _2026-11-01 · realm/blong-agent · open_

The engine result types carry no usage, so a session cannot report tokens in or out and the stats
command can only show turns, steps, tool calls and history size. Add an optional usage object with
input and output tokens to the step and the session result, write it per step on the checkpoint and
aggregate it on the session, and let a harness that does not report it leave it null rather than
guess.

A native copilot run does report something the header throws away: every tool result's
`toolTelemetry.metrics` carries `context_current_tokens` and `context_token_limit` (15461 of 655360
in the tour run, session 784d3115), so the context cell has a real number available from the
telemetry the realm already stores, while tokens in and out still need the usage object. Read the
metrics from the tool-result payload before inventing a second source.

### T-589 — The resume step of test.agent.session reports resumed false

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

The third step of test.agent.session, anAnswerResumesASuspendedSessionExactlyOnce, fails at its own
assertion: agent.answer.receive answers stored true but resumed false. The precondition is that the
session row reads suspended and its workerId equals this host at the moment the answer arrives, and
the step asserts the suspended status just before it, so the cause is one of two things to check in
that order: whether agent.session.get answers the row with the id it was handed after
agentSessionSuspend edited it, and whether the session the step picks when the pool has no third
ticket is the one it suspended. The other two steps pass: a tick claims, runs three scripted turns,
writes a checkpoint per step and two tool events, and an answered question continues the loop. Add a
probe in the step that reads the session through agent.session.get immediately before
agentAnswerReceive and asserts its status and workerId, so the next run names which of the two it is
instead of guessing.

Cause was test data, not the precondition: the check reported already-stored because the prompt id
was a literal reused across runs. A per-run prompt id and a both-shapes transcript reader made all
four steps pass.

### T-717 — Declare the agent realm's vocabulary and convert its call sites

> _2026-11-18 · realm/blong-agent · done_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

The realm is the first place outside the framework that declares a vocabulary, and it proved the
seam — by breaking it in three ways, each fixed where it belonged rather than worked around in the
realm.

`lukaot/error.ts` replaces `error/error.ts`: fourteen entries as clean identifiers
(`agentSessionNotFound`, not `agent.sessionNotFound`), messages written `{sessionId}` instead of
`?sessionId?`, every status code kept (404, 409, 429, 403, 400, 408, 502, 503, 504) and the reason
each is what it is. The derived factory name is unchanged — `errors.errorAgentSessionNotFound` is
what the handlers already called — so no call site moved. `lukaot/signal.ts` declares four signals:
the two the realm's level calls became (`agentAnswerWakeUnpublished`, `agentSessionUnrecoverable`)
and two the worker now announces (`agentTicketClaimed`, `agentSessionResumed`), the second pair
carrying the claim and the resume into a session's flow. The worker also announces two checkpoints —
`agent.ticket.claimed`, `agent.session.resumed` — so a session is drawn from what its worker says,
not only from what a test does.

Three framework faults, found by running it:

- `Kinds` had no `'vocabulary'`, so the loader's `object:vocabulary` case could never match and a
  declaration was silently dropped. The kind is now part of the union and the reason is written
  beside it.
- `Watch` routed a layer file by its _name_, so `lukaot/error.ts` went to the error factory, which
  read the vocabulary's `signal` member as an error type and demanded a message for it. It now
  routes by what the item _is_.
- `layerProxy` deferred a vocabulary to the closure that runs when a layer's methods are registered
  — and `lukaot/` has no methods of its own, so the registration never ran. It registers eagerly
  now.

One more, in the capture seam: `AdapterBase.capture` memoised into a private field, and a port's
`capture` is read through the layer's _proxy_, where a private field lookup throws. It keeps its
resolved surface under a symbol instead, which the proxy forwards.

Test: `test/lukaot.vocabulary.test.ts`, 24 assertions — fourteen codes, no legacy `?name?` left
anywhere, and four messages interpolated through the emitter's own renderer, which is what T-717 was
for: a placeholder nothing supplied used to print, and now the call is what supplies it.

Gates: `realm/blong-agent` 35 assertions, `core/blong-gogo` 1230, lint clean in both.

Vocabulary declared, both log sites converted, claim and resume announced; three loader faults and
one capture-seam fault fixed where they belonged.

### T-718 — Verify the agent signals reach the store, the service and the CLI

> _2026-11-18 · realm/blong-agent · done_

Planned in [#277](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/277).

`test/lukaot.reach.test.ts` proves the three reach points in one process. It boots the realm with
the store in a temporary directory and the service on a port the operating system chooses, schedules
the realm's own groups — `test.agent.session`, `test.agent.recovery` and a new
`test.agent.observability` — and then asks the three questions: does the service list the signal the
tick announced under its declared name; does the flow ledger list the execution that claim belongs
to; and does the line the process printed resolve back through `lukaot inspect` to the record whose
identity is that declared name. 12 assertions.

Reaching them meant fixing four defects the framework could not show on its own, and each was the
failure the task exists to catch. A record the framework wrote carried its identifier as a _field_ —
where the printer reads it — while the service refuses any record whose top-level identity is
missing, so the service had never received a single framework record: no templates, no flows, no
diagrams. A realm-level vocabulary was pushed onto the result of the layer that declared it, which
for `lukaot/` is a layer with no port, so `port.signal` was undefined and every converted call site
was a silent no-op; the realm now owns one array and every layer's result points at it.
`lib .checkpoint`, deliberately undefined outside a recording mode, answered a deferred thunk from
the lib proxy instead of `undefined`, so `lib.checkpoint?.(…)` threw and the tick failed on its
first checkpoint. And a declared error's message was never interpolated on the legacy
`errors.errorXxx` path, which read `params.params` only, so every message printed its `{name}`
placeholders. The realm's own catch compared `code` where a declared error carries `type`, so its
`agentCheckpointMissing` branch had never run.

`core/lukaot/inspect.ts` is no longer a stub: `parseReference` in `refs.ts` beside the writer so the
two share one table, plus `resolveReference`, `inspectLine` and `inspectStore`, with the store
opened read-only because resolving a reference must not be what evicts an entry.

- verify: `cd realm/blong-agent && blong-dev test` passes, 48 assertions; the tick is covered
  to 96.96% of statements. What remains is the ticket's optional chat channel and one range at the
  end of the claim path — pass-through reads of optional fixture data, not logic.

### T-560 — Publish a wake-up on Redis and Kafka

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

Planned in [#299](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/299).

Both brokers are in the cluster, so both are wired. The clients already exist — `adapter.kafka` is a
stream transport over `node-rdkafka` and `adapter.redis` a key/hash/script vocabulary over `ioredis`
— and neither carries a notification: kafka has no `publish` method and redis has neither `publish`
nor `subscribe`. So `adapter/notifyKafka.ts` and `adapter/notifyRedis.ts` are two instances of a
`notify` namespace whose work is the three pieces the transports leave out: a `notify.publish`
handler the answer path calls, a subscription that routes a wake to `agent.answer.wake` (a codec for
kafka's decoded triple, a subscriber loop for redis), and a group id carrying `HOSTNAME` so every
pod sees every wake. A test that needs a broker skips without one (`@@D-709`).

### T-590 — The agent plan's remaining work, in the order to take it

> _2026-10-31 · realm/blong-agent · done_

What is left in the plan ([#299](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/299)), in the order it
should be taken. First `T-574`, the chat seam: the agent realm cannot load chat's simulators because
`realm/blong-chat/package.json` exports only `./server.ts`, so a child
`import('@feasibleone/blong-chat/sim/slackSim.ts')` is blocked by the exports map. The enabler is
one line in that map (the simulator is a reusable test double, like `@feasibleone/blong-test`), then
an agent-side `chat` intent block that lists only `test.agent.chat` in `watch.test` — that intent
separation is required because `questionMethod` is a single port setting and every other group
answers its questions through `test.agent.question.echo`, so a chat-pointed run must schedule the
seam group alone. The group itself starts `agent.session.run` without awaiting it, polls
`agent.checkpoint.last.get` for the pending prompt id, delivers the answer through
`chat.in.answer.receive`, and then awaits the run. Second `T-560`/`T-572`, the notify adapters: both
brokers answer here (6379, 9092) but the Redis adapter has no `pub`/`sub` at all, so that vocabulary
must be added to `core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/server/redis.ts` before a realm instance can
subscribe; Kafka can carry a wake as a triple today. Third `T-578`/`T-579` (a writable claim for the
workspace, a `dshHome` volume, the key as a Secret) and `T-581`, which needs the generator driven
from a suite — `blong ./index.ts k8s` in the realm exits 0 and writes nothing, so the realm entry is
not the place it runs. Then `T-576`/`T-577` for the coverage number and the cross-package run, and
`T-585` if a blog post is wanted.

### T-810 — The session feed group hangs the run and is out of the watch list

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · done_

The group is written (`realm/blong-agent/server/test/test/testAgentSessionFeed.ts`) and left out of
`index.ts`'s watch list because it hangs the whole run: the harness's `platform.test` never returns,
the run dies on tap's 30 s timeout with no step named, and the platform's `stop` never runs. The
watch half is the suspect — `agentSessionWatch` is called through the handler proxy as
`kafkaTopicWatch` is in the perf group, which works there, but this handler is on the `db` port
whose request queue may be held for as long as the stream is open. Check in this order: (1) whether
`ports.agent.request`'s p-queue is concurrency 1 and therefore blocked by a generator that is still
open; (2) whether the abort reaches the inner Kafka watch when it is passed as
`{...$meta, stream: true}` from the handler rather than from the caller; (3) whether the three
consumers the test opens are all closed before the step returns. Put the group back in the watch
list when it is green; the list half (`agent.session.find` with the projection join and `before`
paging) may be split out so a regression in it is not blocked by the streaming question.

Diagnosed and fixed. The group name was the first defect: the file was testAgentSessionFeed.ts,
whose wire name is test.agent.sessionFeed, so the scheduled test.agent.feed resolved to nothing.
Renamed to testAgentFeed.ts. The hang was the Kafka watch: its consumer was closed in the
generator's finally, which never runs when the reader stops without resuming the iterator, so an
aborted reader left its consumer connected (12 established broker connections, process never
exited). topicWatch now closes the consumer on abort, once, still deferred to the next tick (F-835).
The list half also needed a whole-second order and a tie-broken cursor (D-1007), and the group is
back in the watch list and green.

### T-793 — `agent.session.watch` streams the tail and then the live events

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-agent · done_

The handler is an async iterable behind `stream: true`. It resolves the partition (session row, else
`topic.partition`), computes `max(low, high - tail)`, yields the filtered batch, then keeps yielding
live batches until `$meta.abort`. `details: false` sends `{partition, offset, size}` and no events.

(`@@D-949`).

  `details: false` carries no events. It skips when the broker does not answer.

Implemented as realm/blong-agent/adapter/db/agentSessionWatch.ts over
sessionFeedStart/sessionFeedFrame: tail from the session's remembered partition (every partition
when the row remembers none), live frames until abort, details:false sending only the cursor and the
size, reachedStart on the first frame. Verified by test.agent.feed's watchTail: the tail in order, a
live record produced while open, the truthful reachedStart flag, the cursor-only mode, and a resume
from a token that skips the record already rendered.

### T-816 — Move the answer wake's subscription into an orchestrator, so an adapter stops calling one

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · done_

`adapter/notify/notifyAnswerWake.ts` is the one edge left where an adapter calls an orchestrator: a
broker hands the wake to the port that listens, and the port forwards it to `agent.answer.wake`
(`@@D-1013`). It is allowed because it decides nothing, but it is still the weaker shape. The better
one is the subscription living in an orchestrator: an orchestrator handler that opens the wake
subscription in its `start()` and dispatches `agent.answer.wake` itself, the way
`orchestrator/agentDispatch.ts` already owns the worker's clock and the way `agent.session.watch`
owns the read stream. What it needs: the subscription methods the adapter currently gets from
`extends: 'adapter.kafka'` must be reachable from the orchestrator through the qualified-name proxy,
and a test that shows a wake delivered with no adapter handler in the path. Do not add a second
forwarding adapter before that is done — the pattern is the cheap shape, and a second copy is how it
becomes the normal one.

Done: the subscription is the dispatch orchestrator's. agentDispatch opens notify.sub.watch in
ready() and dispatches agent.answer.wake for each message; adapter/notify/notifyAnswerWake.ts is
deleted; the redis adapter answers a {ns}.sub.watch iterable so a caller reads the channel instead
of being called back. The channel is a setting (wake.channel, set by the notify intent), the publish
in agentAnswerReceive reads the same setting, and test.agent.notify proves it: a wake resumes a
parked session with no adapter handler in the path, and a call to notify.answer.wake is now refused
(D-1015).

### T-819 — A native run's metric counts one turn and no tools, so the header reads zero

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · done_

A native (copilot) run leaves a metric that says nothing happened: session `49a688d1` wrote five
events — `text`, `tool`, `tool-result`, `text`, `step` — and the page drew the tool card with its 77
ms, while `agent_sessionMetric` recorded `turnCount 1, messageTokens 0, toolCount 0, toolsJSON {}`
and the header reported zero tokens and zero tool time. So the projection counts a native run's
turns but neither its calls nor their durations, and the tokens it never sees because the copilot
events carry no usage; the step engine's `toolCall`/`toolEvent` shape is the only one it recognises.
That is worth fixing before the page is trusted for a real task, because "how long did the tools
take and what did it cost" is the question the header exists to answer — either the copilot kind
should emit the same tool event the step engine does, or `agentMetricProject` should read the
`tool`/`tool-result` pair this engine writes.

Fixed where the T-819 note suggested it should be: the copilot kind now keeps the calls that have
started and attaches the tool's name and the measured duration to the completion event it reports
and records, so a projection and a page read one shape whichever engine wrote it. Verified on a the
second runtime, agent_sessionMetric holds agent_sessionMetric holds toolCount 2 with
{"create":{count:1,durationMs:58},"bash":{...}}, and the page header reads TOOLS 2 · TOOL TIME 143
ms where it read 0 before. Tokens stay a separate fact: the harness streams whole messages and no
deltas, so the header says so (T-820).

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · done_

Runtime 1.0.114 sends no delta events: the narration between tool calls and the reasoning before

for deltas showed twelve tool calls with nothing between them. Both are now reported whole when the
runtime streams no deltas, and a delta is used where one exists. The same probe found the shapes a
row needs and the page did not read: a shell answer carries `shellExecution.exitCode` and a

lines, a read returns the file as `content` and a diff-shaped snapshot in `detailedContent`, and a

text, and a question as a card with its choices and answer. The adapter also reports
`assistant.usage` on the finished state, which is the token and context number the header had been
showing as an em dash.

Copilot narration and reasoning are reported whole where a runtime sends no deltas; usage rides the
finished state; a tool section keeps a detail read from its payloads and the page draws shell,

sessionMessages.ts maps the rows onto the chat view's user/assistant/reasoning/activity shape, with

### T-827 — A success is a tick, a slow call is the only time, and a silent command shows no JSON

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · done_

Reading the first real tour in the page showed four things that were technically correct and
practically noise. A shell whose payload the page understood still fell back to its raw result when
the output was empty, so `sleep 15` was drawn with a JSON envelope containing the runtime's own
`<shellId: … completed with exit code 0>` trailer under it. Every successful command carried a
bordered pill reading `✓ 0`, which is most of the marks on a page where the one failure is what a
reader has to find. Every call carried a duration, so `0 ms` sat beside the quick ones and the
forty-five-second command had to be hunted. Every foldable section drew its caret permanently, and
thinking wore a heading reading `reasoning` on a tinted box of its own.

The page now shows a bare tick for a zero exit and keeps the pill and the number for a failure;
shows no time under a second, counts the rest in seconds and minutes, and marks anything over thirty
seconds; draws a caret only under the pointer and while the section it opened is open; and draws
thinking as an icon over italic muted prose with no title and no surface. A lone call is now the
same card a run holds, rather than a section that printed its arguments as JSON again.

A zero exit is a bare tick, a failure keeps its pill and its number, a time under a second is not
drawn and one over thirty is marked, a caret appears on hover and stays while the section it opened
is open, thinking is an icon over italic prose with no title or surface, a lone call is the same
card a run holds, and an understood shell never falls back to its JSON. The browser spec expands a
shell, an edit, a read, a question and a write and pins every one of those marks in both palettes.

### T-826 — The browser spec attaches to a dev server on 8080 and waits for a seed that server never ran

> _2026-11-25 · realm/blong-agent · done_

`test/agentSession.play.ts` reads the list from `agent.session.find`, and the `playwright` intent
seeds a session at boot through `test.agent.ui`. Locally the spec sat for thirty seconds on a row
that was never written and failed on its first assertion.

The cause was the run, not the seed: the factory sets `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` on the
backend port, and a dev backend was already listening on the default 8080 — started with
`microservice integration dev`, which has no `playwright` intent, so it neither seeds the
conversation nor serves the ring the page reads. Playwright attached to that server, the seed group
never ran, and the list answered with sessions from the developer's own runs. Running the suite on
its own ports (`PLAYWRIGHT_BACKEND_PORT=8091 PLAYWRIGHT_FRONTEND_PORT=5191`) starts a fresh server,
the seed runs, and the spec passes: both palettes, every card, every mark.

What is left is to make the reuse safe rather than documented: a suite that attaches to a foreign
server should say so — the seeded row is the natural probe, and a message naming the port and the
intents that server is running would save the next reader the thirty seconds. The row is also found
by its title now, so a real run that is merely newer no longer shadows it.

The backend port is reused when it already answers, and a dev backend started without the playwright
intent neither seeds the conversation nor serves the ring: the suite ran against it and waited
thirty seconds for a row nobody wrote. On its own ports a fresh server seeds and the spec passes, in
both palettes, with every card expanded. A probe that names the port and its intents when the seeded
row is absent is left as the improvement.

with visibly different token colours.

The spec captures the same transcript in the light palette, asserts the wrapper class and that a
code comment's colour changed, and both pictures are checked in. It runs on its own ports, which is
what made it runnable at all (see T-826).
